title: Quarterly cadence protocol - Harmonize Hosted API commitments with Model Catalog rotation
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Purpose: Establish a repeatable quarterly cadence (protocol) that ties Hosted API endpoint commitments to model catalog rotation windows, evaluation gates, and operational readiness checks. Scope: Q2 roadmap planning across Hosted API commit lanes (core, convergence, exploratory) and model catalog lifecycle activities (onboarding, staged rotation, deprecation). This ticket defines deliverables for PM, Eng, Design, and Research to produce a single quarterly commit schedule and a lightweight decision rubric for last-minute model swaps.

Objectives:
- Produce a single calendar with tranche dates for canaries, capacity hedges, regression windows, and rollback cutoffs.
- Define acceptance criteria for adding/removing a model from Hosted endpoints (perf, cost, eval pass/fail, compatibility).
- Standardize how OKRs map to model rotations (which rotations are OKR-driven vs. ops-driven).
- Reduce cross-team review cycles by 30% via a delegated decision rubric and a pre-approved contingency matrix.

Acceptance criteria:
- Calendar published in Drive + linked to Console release lanes.
- Decision rubric doc with sign-off from Eng Lead (runtime), Research, and Security.
- Two sample model rotations scheduled and executed in staging using the new cadence.
- Post-rotation monitoring playbook stub created for SRE/Console.

Stakeholders: PM (Asha Patel, Marcus Nguyen), Eng (runtime, infra, SLO), Research (evals), Design (console UX), GTM (docs + comms).

Key trade-offs discussed:
- Frequency of rotations vs. eval cost: more frequent rotations improve freshness but increase eval compute spend and risk surface. Recommendation: triage by customer impact and replace only models that provide >=10% improvement on key tasks or reduce cost per token by >=15% after quantization.
- Canary window length: longer windows catch regressions but delay feature parity. Start with a 48h canary for core lanes, 24h for convergence lanes.

Dependencies: ["ENG-1842", "ENG-40221", "PM-30921"],

Risks:
- Late-breaking model regressions during high-traffic windows (mitigation: pre-canary shadow traffic and auto-fallback policy).
- Misalignment on SLO ownership between runtime and Hosted operations (mitigation: explicit SLO owner in rubric).

Deliverables and timeline:
- Week 1 (Feb 9-15): Align stakeholders, draft calendar and rubric.
- Week 2 (Feb 16-22): Iterate with Eng on canary mechanics and fallback.
- Week 3 (Feb 23-Mar 1): Dry-run two model rotations in staging.
- Week 4 (Mar 2-8): Publish calendar, runbook, and annotate Console release lanes.

Links and artifacts:
- Draft rubric (Drive): https://drive.google.com/hostedapi-model-rubric-draft
- Staging runbook (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PM/pages/quarterly-cadence-protocol
- Example PR (runtime): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821
- Canary dashboard (Console): https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/canary-rotations

Notes on OKR linkage:
- Rotation activities tagged as either OKR-MUST (directly tied to revenue/partner commitments) or OKR-NICE (quality/cost improvements). Only OKR-MUST rotations get accelerated windows; others follow regular cadence.

Next steps:
1) PM to send calendar + meeting invite to runtime and research owners (this ticket).
2) Eng to produce a short spec for auto-fallback behavior for model swaps (ENG follow-up).
3) Research to seed evaluation tests for the two staging rotations.

Customer impact: medium
